title_eng: Investigation of Photoplethysmography AC Component Variation Before and After Surgery

Abstract—The purpose of this study was to investigate 
whether PPG AC waveforms significantly changed by pain. To 
estimate PPG AC changes, we propose d new features, 
ACVsystole/ACA and ACVdiastole/ACA, that divide systolic and 
diastolic AC peak by AC amplitude, respectively, and applied 
them to the dataset before and after surgery to verify the 
statistical difference. As a result, both proposed parameters 
showed significant differences (P<0.001) between the pre- and 
postoperative data sets. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Pain can stimulate the autonomic nervous system and 
contribute to vasodilation and vasoconstriction by vagus nerve 
stimulation. Photoplethysmography (PPG), a non-invasive 
method for measuring blood volume change, is a promising 
method of non-invasive pain quantification [1]. Amplitude of 
PPG waveform is proportional to the blood volume, thus vaso-
motion and ANS activity could be inferred from PPG 
amplitude changes. Moreover, PPG waveform provide 
systolic and diastolic phase information. In view of vasomotor 
tone, systolic and diastolic phase may provide useful 
information. This study aims to investigate the waveform of 
PPG and to find useful index for pain quantification. From the 
above viewpoint, we analyze the AC amplitude and AC 
variation of PPG waveform and investigate whether it can be 
used as an indicator of pain. 
II. MATERIALS AND METHODS 
Sixty surgical patients (29 males, 31 females, 52.1 ± 11.4 
years old) were enrolled to the experiment, and 58 pair of 
dataset was used except 2 pair of dataset which has recording 
error. Every systolic and diastolic peak location was manually 
found by proficient experts after applying automatic peak 
detection algorithm. In this study, changes in amplitude of 
PPG due to pain were observed through the AC amplitude

dataset was used except 2 pair of dataset which has recording 
error. Every systolic and diastolic peak location was manually 
found by proficient experts after applying automatic peak 
detection algorithm. In this study, changes in amplitude of 
PPG due to pain were observed through the AC amplitude

Therefore, the variations of the systolic and diastolic peak 
amplitude were normalized by using the AC amplitude of PPG 
(ACA). Finally, we derived two parameters as follows ; 
ACVsystole/ACA and ACVdiastole/ACA shown in Fig. 1. To 
validate the significance of difference statistically, we 
calculated ACVsystole/ACA and ACVdiastole/ACA from dataset of 
before and after surgery and applied paired t-test or Wilcoxon 
signed rank test by its normality. 
III. RESULTS AND DISCUSSIONS 
Fig. 2 shows the fractional change of derived parameters 
before and after surgery. In this results, significant changes 
(P<0.001) in pain were observed in both presented parameters, 
ACVsystole/ACA and ACVdiastole/ACA. The result of this study 
suggests that changes in PPG AC amplitude may be equal or 
increased by pain stimuli, given previous studies suggesting 
that PPG amplitude decreases with pain [1]. 
IV. CONCLUSION 
The new parameters presented in this study show 
significant differences according to pain. We expect that these 
new approaches would contribute for pain quantification.
